actions: Offer to cook dinner; check what she would enjoy before starting.
Wash the dishes and put them away without leaving the last step to her.
Complete your agreed share of laundry, including folding and putting it away.
Pick up the groceries you agreed on; ask before substituting items.
Prepare breakfast if welcome, and clean up afterwards.
Prepare your own things for tomorrow so the morning needs less coordination.
Take out the rubbish and replace the bag.
Clear one shared surface without moving her personal belongings.
Offer to take one agreed errand off her list.
Ask whether carrying the heavy bags would help; accept her answer.
Offer water or a familiar drink and let her choose.
Handle the details of an agreed journey, including the way home.
Do your share of a household task so she can take a break if she wants.
Fix one small household annoyance you have already agreed to address.
Store the leftovers and leave the kitchen ready for the next meal.
Check shared bathroom supplies and replace what is running out.
Offer to change the bed linen; agree on timing first.
Suggest a short walk with an easy route and an easy option to decline.
Choose two realistic dinner options and let her say what suits her.
Finish one administrative task that is your responsibility.
Tidy your shoes and belongings from the entrance.
Split a large shared task into steps and complete your agreed part.
Offer to prepare a snack or packed lunch using her preferences.
Finish one small thing you promised, then say it is done.
support: Ask: “Would you like listening, ideas, or practical help?”
Put your phone aside and listen without preparing a reply.
Ask: “What would make this evening easier for you?”
Reflect what you heard, then check you understood correctly.
Say: “We can change the plan if it no longer works for you.”
Ask whether she would prefer company or some time alone.
Name one effort you noticed and thank her specifically for it.
Ask which part of the day was hardest; let her decide how much to share.
Say: “You do not have to explain everything right now.”
Offer a hug as a question, and accept either answer warmly.
Ask what she would like you to remember for next time.
Acknowledge her feeling without telling her how she should feel.
Say: “I can handle my part; you do not need to remind me.”
Ask whether she wants a check-in later or would rather initiate it.
Name a quality you admire and a recent example of it.
Thank her for something ordinary that often goes unnoticed.
Ask: “Is there something you want to celebrate today?”
Let her finish her sentence before asking your next question.
Say: “I hear that this matters to you.”
Ask whether she wants reassurance or space to think.
Mention a moment when her care made a difference to you.
Share one thing you appreciate about your time together.
Ask what kind of help she does not want today.
Say when you are available to talk, and keep that time free.
context: Her stated wellbeing matters more than the calendar estimate.
A changed plan does not require an explanation about hormones.
An offer is useful only when “no” is a real option.
Do not turn practical help into a request for praise or affection.
Ask before touching or moving personal belongings.
Different preferences do not mean that either person is wrong.
Do not infer a mood from the estimated cycle phase.
Keep private cycle information private unless she agrees otherwise.
A promise is easier to trust when you give a realistic time.
Finish the task rather than leaving the organising to her.
Ask one clear question instead of repeatedly checking on her.
Silence can be comfortable; check before trying to fill it.
You can listen carefully without agreeing on every detail.
Pause a tense discussion and agree when to return to it.
Do not use this app to win an argument.
An apology names your action and the repair you will make.
A good day does not create an obligation to be social or intimate.
You can offer support without taking over her decisions.
Respect a boundary even when you do not understand its reason.
Do not share her personal experience as a joke.
Notice what worked and ask before repeating it another day.
Keep your own responsibilities visible and manageable.
If you misunderstood, ask calmly rather than guessing intent.
Small reliable actions matter more than a grand promise.

menstrual: If she wants period supplies, check her preferred product and bring exactly that.
Offer to empty the bathroom bin discreetly; keep her belongings private.
If she reports discomfort, offer her usual comfort item; otherwise take an ordinary chore.
Ask whether an easier meal would help during her period; follow her actual appetite.
follicular: Offer one small step in a project she has chosen; do not assume extra energy.
Suggest an activity she enjoys and leave the pace to her.
Ask whether she wants to plan an outing; staying home is equally valid.
Make space for her chosen hobby by completing your own household task.
mid_cycle: Suggest time together without treating an estimated phase as consent.
Ask what kind of closeness she wants; a quiet evening is a complete answer.
Help organise a date you both want, with room to change the plan.
Protect agreed personal time instead of assuming she wants company.
luteal: Before the estimated period, ask whether her usual supplies need restocking.
Offer to prepare an agreed meal ahead so the evening is less rushed.
If she asks for a lighter schedule, handle one practical rearrangement.
Review your share of upcoming chores without assuming how she feels.
